top_five.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, with over 4,400 deaths reported amid widespread unmonitored community transmission and cross-border spread.
The World Health Organization warned that ongoing Israeli blockades and humanitarian aid restrictions are driving a man-made mass starvation crisis across the Gaza Strip.
Energy ceasefire negotiations between Russia and Ukraine collapsed as Moscow launched record drone attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure and Kyiv resumed strikes on Russian refineries.
Suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled over three weeks to more than 8,000 cases this year, heavily concentrated among displaced families in overcrowded southwestern governorates.
Deepening poverty in Afghanistan now affects an estimated 28 million people due to mass returns from neighboring countries, persistent drought, and severe international aid cuts.

top_story.quote: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is confronting the fastest-growing and deadliest Ebola outbreak in its history, with confirmed cases surpassing 9,000 and fatalities exceeding 4,400 as ongoing violence and high mobility hamper containment efforts.
top_story.label: AFRICA — DR Congo Ebola Outbreak

Middle East.headline: Gaza/OPT — WHO warns of man-made mass starvation crisis
Middle East.body: The World Health Organization warned that the Gaza Strip is facing a man-made mass starvation crisis resulting from ongoing Israeli blockades and restrictions on humanitarian aid. Essential supplies including food, water, and medical aid remain blocked outside the enclave, leading to depleted food reserves following a full blockade imposed in March. More than 100 aid organizations issued a joint plea regarding the worsening hunger crisis. WHO officials stated the emergency is directly driven by human actions.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Cholera cases triple amid expanding displacement
Middle East.body: Suspected cholera cases in Yemen tripled over a three-week period as ongoing conflict forces families into overcrowded displacement camps, according to the World Health Organization. Weekly suspected cases surged from 217 in early September to 647 by early October. Yemen has recorded 8,034 suspected cases and 27 deaths this year, with a quarter occurring in the past month. Approximately 92 percent of cases are concentrated in five southwestern governorates hosting large displaced populations, while remote camps in Hadramout face severe medical access constraints.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Escalating clashes in Taiz force mass displacement
Middle East.body: Intense clashes between government-aligned forces and Houthi fighters along the perimeter of Taiz city and the southern Sabr Al-Mawadim district have caused widespread insecurity, forcing thousands of families to flee their homes. Local reports indicate that renewed military engagements have rendered frontlines around Taiz increasingly volatile, driving a surge in forced displacement as affected populations flee the escalating violence.

Middle East.headline: Lebanon/Israel — Israeli defense chief warns of potential mass displacement
Middle East.body: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz warned that Hezbollah would face severe military action and permanent loss of territory in southern Lebanon, including the Nabatieh and Litani River areas, if it joins an Iranian attack against Israel. During a visit to the border buffer zone, Katz stated that the military is prepared for a ground offensive and threatened the total evacuation of Beirut's southern suburb of Dahiyeh, warning that more than one million residents could be displaced.

Americas.headline: Mexico — Hurricane Simon and storm remnants trigger deadly coastal flooding
Americas.body: Heavy rainfall from Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel triggered flooding and landslides along Mexico’s Pacific coast. The storm system affected several states, including Guerrero, Nayarit, Sinaloa, and Baja California. In the coastal city of Ensenada, floodwaters swept away vehicles, while outer storm bands battered communities near Puerto Vallarta. Authorities confirmed at least five to six deaths linked to the weather conditions. Although Hurricane Simon subsequently weakened while moving slowly offshore, emergency officials warned that flooding risks, high surf, and potential evacuations remained active concerns for communities in Baja California Sur.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Humanitarian cash assistance delivered following twin earthquakes
Americas.body: Humanitarian organization GiveDirectly reported delivering cash transfers to 3,765 people affected by twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24. The 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes heavily impacted areas including La Guaira. Cash distributions were processed via Venezuela’s Pago Móvil digital payment network, with initial transfers beginning 21 days after the disaster. Each recipient received $340, with half of recipients using the funds for basic necessities like food and water, and 60% using the money to maintain or restart income-generating activities.

Africa.headline: DR Congo Ebola death toll passes 4,400 in record-breaking outbreak
Africa.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the fastest-growing on record, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC). The outbreak began in May and has caused 9,144 confirmed cases and 4,410 deaths, according to figures the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published on Wednesday. Caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, it is now the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. Africa.headline: WHO raises alarm as undetected Ebola community deaths fuel DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
Africa.body: The World Health Organization has warned that undetected community deaths are accelerating the spread of the Bundibugyo Ebola strain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as confirmed cases surge past 9,000 with over 4,300 fatalities. With nearly one-third of new cases identified only after death, health authorities are struggling to contain an epidemic that has now spread across seven provinces, exposing severe limitations in rural healthcare access and outbreak surveillance in one of Africa's most complex operational environments. Europe.headline: Russia and Ukraine resume energy strikes despite Trump warnings
Europe.body: Moscow sends swarms of drones to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine as Zelenskyy says Kyiv will restart strikes on Russian oil refineries Europe live – latest updates The White House’s unilateral effort to negotiate an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine has collapsed as Moscow sent a record swarm of drones overnight to attack infrastructure in central Ukraine and Kyiv appeared to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries – despite warnings from Donald Trump. Moscow accused Ukraine of launching its first strike against a Russian oil refinery in the Ryazan region since Trump abruptly declared an “energy ceasefire” that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to .

Europe.headline: Restrictions expose Ukraine's Starlink dependency in Russia war
Europe.body: Restrictions reported by Ukraine on its use of the US satellite internet system Starlink have exposed Kyiv's reliance on the technology for both offensive and defensive operations in its fight against Russia'a invasion, analysts and observers say. A senior Ukrainian official, who asked not to be named, told AFP on Wednesday that Starlink data communication speeds had been "throttled". The change has come at a time of renewed tension between Kyiv and Washington, with US President Donald Trump seeking to bring down global fuel prices by buying Russian diesel and pressuring both sides to stop attacking energy infrastructure.

Europe.headline: Thursday briefing: Thanks to an erratic Trump, peace in Ukraine is still far away
Europe.body: In today’s newsletter: As Russia resists a ceasefire and Trump’s shifting priorities unsettle allies, an end to the conflict isn’t getting any closer Good morning. In his usual asinine unconventional approach to international relations, Donald Trump announced on Sunday (via Truth Social, how else) an “ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine”, apparently without checking with either side. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said any such deal was “news to me,” nonetheless declared he was “ready and we will accept it”. Vladimir Putin responded by blowing up some Ukrainian power plants. This has been the tenor of much diplomacy during Trump’s tenure: false starts, U-turns, incoherent positions (and some playful flirting with Vlad).

Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Asia-Pacific.headline: Pakistan school roof collapse kills dozens of pupils, teacher in Peshawar
Asia-Pacific.body: A teacher and twenty-seven pupils were killed when a school roof collapsed in the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar on Thursday, a hospital official said. More than thirty people were injured, with six of them believed to be in a critical condition.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DR Congo/Kenya — Major Ebola Outbreak Spreads Cross-Border
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The World Health Organization warned of undetected Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain continues to worsen. Over 9,000 cases and 4,300 deaths have been recorded across seven provinces, with a case-fatality rate near 50 percent. A significant proportion of fatalities are occurring in communities rather than treatment centers, indicating unmonitored transmission. The outbreak has also spread to Kenya, where health authorities confirmed a second linked infection in a quarantined relative of the index case. No approved vaccine currently exists specifically for the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nepal — Displacement from Flooding Suspends Child Immunization Campaign
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A planned measles-rubella vaccination campaign in Nepal's flood-affected districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading has been put on hold because health authorities cannot locate displaced children. Families remain scattered following the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods due to delays in official rehabilitation efforts. Officials from the Department of Health Services stated that the lack of accurate information on the whereabouts and living conditions of displaced children prevents the immediate launch of the immunization drive, heightening disease risks among vulnerable populations.
